Requested service: Knee arthroscopy with partial meniscectomy  
CPT: 29881  
Provider: Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery  

Dear MVP Appeals Department:

I am appealing MVP Health Care’s denial dated August 13, 2026, of prior authorization for knee arthroscopy and meniscus surgery under CPT 29881. The stated reason was that the submitted clinical records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery.

The records do document extensive conservative treatment:

- I have experienced progressive knee pain for approximately 12 months, despite rest.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy from April 8, 2026, through July 15, 2026. The treatment focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, and I completed 24 visits. This treatment is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for approximately eight months, with inadequate relief.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 10, 2026. It produced only approximately four weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, I continue to experience pain, locking, and giving way. I cannot squat or kneel and am limited to level walking. Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side, and range of motion is limited by pain.

The MRI performed on July 2, 2026, provides a structural explanation for the persistent symptoms. It shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. The MRI also shows preserved articular cartilage and only Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes. These findings support treatment directed at the displaced meniscal tear rather than continued treatment for advanced degenerative arthritis.

The requested surgery is medically necessary because the meniscal tear is displaced and causing mechanical locking and functional impairment, and because symptoms have persisted despite prolonged medication treatment, a substantial course of supervised physical therapy, rest, and a corticosteroid injection. The clinical record therefore addresses the denial reason by documenting both the duration of conservative care and the inadequate response to it.

The record also documents the absence of identified factors that would otherwise make the requested procedure inappropriate: there is no active infection or untreated substance use; BMI is 29; and I am a non-smoker.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for CPT 29881. Please have the reviewer consider the complete physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection history, July 2, 2026 MRI report, examination findings, and the orthopedic surgery documentation from Duval, MD.

I also request that MVP provide the exact medical-necessity policy and clinical-review criteria used for this determination, including the applicable policy title, policy number, version or effective date, and the specific criteria applied to CPT 29881. The publicly retrievable materials did not identify the specific policy document or policy text governing this denial, so no plan policy language is quoted in this appeal.

Please send the appeal determination and the requested criteria in writing. If additional information is needed, please contact me or my treating provider.

Sincerely,

Cameron Brooks  
Member ID: W412154328  
[Telephone Number]
